location: San Antonio, Texas — saloon interior hung with trophy heads (“Union Bar”)
recipient: Mrs. A.H.S. Peak, Bluffs, Illinois, R.F.D. #2
notes: Front: interior photo of a saloon densely hung floor-to-ceiling with mounted deer, antelope, and elk heads and antler racks, a “UNION BAR” sign visible among the trophies, ornate cash registers on the counter — unidentified, but consistent with early-1900s San Antonio saloon photography (possibly the famous Buckhorn Saloon, though not confirmed). Published by Dahrooge Post Card Co. 1¢ green stamp; San Antonio, Texas postmark, May 29, 1913, 11:09 AM. Message: “San Antonio, May 29th. Dear Folks at Home: I leave here to-night (Thursday) for Parsons. Have been in a dreadful stew getting ready to go. Will write you from Aunt Mattie's. Don't feel uneasy about my just writing — love to all, [signature illegible].”

location: Erlangen, Germany — amateur radio QSL card to Anchorage, Alaska
address: westl. Stadtmauerstraße 19, Erlangen, Germany (US Occupation Zone)
sender: Werner Koch — station DA2AY (ex Ym4ay), nickname “Micky”
recipient: Nicholas, operator of shortwave station KL7BE, Anchorage, Alaska
notes: Front: printed shortwave QSL card for station DEM=6182 / DA2AY (5 watts), confirming a CW contact with KL7BE (Anchorage) on 14 Mc on Dec 1, 1948 at 0820 GMT, signal report RST 449, weather “foggy.” Operator asks KL7BE to relay a QSL to neighboring station KL7SS (“Frank”) and requests one in return for his HAZ-Diplom award. Distributed via the WBRC-Stuttgart QSL bureau, Box 585. Back (handwritten, in English): “Dear Nicholas! Suppose you have German blood in your arteries? Your name seems so German-like. I found your address in the 1947 call-book edition. Hope to serve you with this report and would be very glad about your QSL, for I need it for one — HAZ-Diplom!! I was licensed in 1937–1939 as a junior operator, stopped [word unclear — possibly flying/service-related] in 1945, and am now on the air as DA2AY. I've called today your neighbor KL7SS but he didn't come back, sorry — I send a QSL also for him, please mediate this card for him, ok! So, I hope to hear from you soon. Wish a very merry X-mas and a Happy New Year! Vy 73's & cheerio! Werner Koch (‘Micky’).” A rare glimpse of postwar amateur radio operators in occupied Germany rebuilding transatlantic contacts.

location: June Lake, California — Rustic June Lake Lodge, June Lake Loop
address: June Lake Lodge, June Lake, California (Mono County, Eastern Sierra)
recipient: Mr. & Mrs. M.F. Weckel, 645 N. Broadview, Wichita, Kansas 67208
notes: Front: color photo of the rustic June Lake Lodge, red roof and green trim against a Sierra Nevada backdrop. Caption: ‘Rustic June Lake Lodge. World's largest four-sided fireplace. Famous landmark on the scenic June Lake Loop Highway. Breathtaking view of Gull and June Lake, and the High Sierras. Open the year around.’ Color photo by Louis & Virginia Kay. 4¢ Lincoln stamp; June Lake, CA postmark, Aug 21, 1967. Message: “Mon. Aug 21-67. Dear Ones! We arrived here last nite from Yosemite. It's beautiful today, snow on the mts around. We are staying at the old Lodge, which has been remodeled so nicely & we are in the same room we have had several times before, overlooking the lakes & village. Will write again soon. Love, [signature illegible].”

location: Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming — Lower Falls, viewed from Uncle Tom's Trail
year: 1969 (trip through Lander & Dubois, WY, and Missoula, MT; postmarked Boardman, Oregon)
sender: [signature illegible — message mentions Eldon, Duke, and Floyd]
recipient: Mr. & Mrs. A.C. Wright, Box 236, Laramie, Wyoming
notes: Front: vertical color photo of the 308-foot Lower Falls of the Yellowstone River. Caption: ‘Lower Falls of the Yellowstone, Yellowstone National Park, from below. Uncle Toms Trail leads to the bottom of the canyon where one gets a splendid view of this tremendous, 308-foot falls.’ Haynes Inc., Yellowstone National Park; Plastichrome by Colourpicture, Boston. 5¢ Washington stamp; postmarked Boardman, Oregon, 1969. Message, written over two days: “Missoula, Mont. Thurs. night / Fri.-noon Boardman, Oreg. Hi — Got to the Park [Thurs?]. Come by Lander & Dubois. Saw some of Park yest. & finished this A.M., went through earthquake area & on up here tonight. Went through Limestone Cone & got here at 7:00. Eldon called & son Duke & they went to the show. Saw 3 bear, lots of elk in Park & 3 moose. Floyd is having a ball! [signature illegible].” The “earthquake area” likely refers to the 1959 Hebgen Lake earthquake zone near West Yellowstone.

location: Southern Arizona, near Tucson — “Family Group of Saguaros”
address: Southern Arizona (message mentions Nogales and Green Valley)
recipient: Mr. & Mrs. M.F. Heckel [likely “Weckel” — matches the address on other cards in this batch], 645 N. Broadview, Wichita, Kansas 67208
notes: Front: wide desert landscape with tall saguaro and cholla cacti against a blue, cloud-studded sky. Caption: ‘Family Group of Saguaros. Symbolic of the desert and all its mystery are the Giant Cacti, whose grotesque silhouettes add character to the Southern Arizona landscape. They attain heights of 50 feet and the ages of some have been estimated at 250 years. The blossom of the Saguaro is the State Flower of Arizona.’ Ray Manley photo, Petley Studios, Phoenix. 9¢ ‘Right of People Peaceably to Assemble’ stamp; Arizona postmark, March 1978. Message: “These stand like guards all around Tucson. We are having a great time. It's raining today — taking a break to write. Went to Nogales yesterday & Green Valley, a retirement city. Also [mission name unclear]. Hard to believe that there is snow on the mtns 30 min up from here. Thank you for thinking of Matt in such a nice way — Love, Mary.” Signed by the same “Mary” who also wrote the 1989 Banff Springs Hotel card in this batch — both addressed to the same Wichita, Kansas family.

location: Banff, Alberta, Canada — The Banff Springs Hotel
recipient: Mr. & Mrs. M.F. Weckel, 645 N. Broadview, Wichita, Kansas 67208, U.S.A.
notes: Front: color photo of the chateau-style Banff Springs Hotel amid dense pine forest. Caption: ‘The Banff Springs Hotel — The original C.P.R. Hotel built on this site was a magnificent wooden structure designed by Bruce Price and built in 1888. The present Rundle stone structure, designed by Walter Painter and J.W. Orrock, was built during and after World War 1, following fires which destroyed part of the original structure.’ © Stephen Hutchings; pub. Altitude Publishing, Banff. 44¢ Canada ‘Atlantic Walrus’ stamp; Canadian postmark, July 28, 1989. Message: “We didn't stay here, but we did stop & go thru it. Very elegant! Butchart Gardens are so beautiful they're beyond description. The train ride was a nice experience & scenery was beautiful. Hope all is well at home. Hug Baby an extra time. Love, Mary.” Same sender (“Mary”) and same Wichita, Kansas recipients as the 1978 Saguaros card in this batch — a recurring family correspondent documenting her travels over at least an 11-year span.

year: Undated (no postmark; sender's note reads “wrote on wrong card” — apparently never mailed)
recipient: Rojana Seaman, 10610 Kentucky, Kansas City, Missouri
notes: Front: photo of the causeway/freeway bridge linking Galveston to the mainland. Caption: ‘Galveston's Two-Mile-Long Causeway Linking Galveston to the Mainland on the Galveston-Houston Freeway.’ Galveston News Co., Curteichcolor. No stamp or postmark — a note at the bottom reads “(wrote on wrong card),” suggesting the sender mis-wrote this one and it was kept rather than mailed. Message: “Wed. – 7:30 P.M. Galveston, Tex. Dear Rojana! We just came across on this ferry boat. We came from Port Arthur, going to Houston. Hope to start home in 3 or 4 days. Rainy & stormy here, getting ready to rain again. We won't see the Gulf anymore, drove a long way by it this p.m. Tell you all about everything when get home. Hope Papa & everyone is O.K. Love, Erna.”
